::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 6th 1893  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS University of Iowa; MsL/Y56se
:::

My dear [Lady Sophia](people/person_1133.qmd),
I am asked to send this card, in case [Lord Selborne](people/person_1129.qmd) has a vote disengaged for this poor young man. I hope the Blind are not so plentiful as idiots and incurables from whom there is no peace![^1]

I suppose you have Dr Pusey’s [life](other_books/otherbook_683.qmd), it must be wonderfully interesting but it has not yet come in my way.[^2] It seems to fill up the complement of the other lives - I remember hearing about [Lucy Pusey](people/person_1216.qmd)’s death.<sup>3</sup> She must have been the flower of the flock.

Yours very sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: No doubt the Earl of Selborne was a subscriber to an institution for the blind, perhaps the [Hampshire Blind School](organizations/other_25.qmd).
[^2]: Pusey’s eldest child Lucy Maria Bouverie Pusey (?1829-22 April 1844).
